intro: Employers' liability insurance is a legal requirement for most UK employers, and searching for it near you usually means you want a local broker who understands your trade and can sort cover without fuss. Whether you have just taken on your first member of staff or you are reviewing a policy that no longer fits, a broker can explain what the law requires and find a quote for you. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK insurance broker, who will quote you directly — price on application.
need_heading: What people searching for employers' liability cover usually need
need_lead: Most people typing this search are employers who want to get the legal side right and understand what they are buying.
needs: You have just hired your first employee and need to arrange cover before they start work.
You run a small trade or shop and want a local broker who can talk through your risks face to face.
Your current policy is up for renewal and you want to compare what is available in your area.
You have taken on staff for the first time after working alone and are unsure what the law expects of you.
You want someone to explain the exclusions and how claims from injured or ill employees would be handled.
context: Employers' liability insurance is legally required for most UK employers, covering claims from employees who are injured or made ill at work. The minimum level of cover is set by law, and you should display your certificate where staff can see it. Fines can apply if you employ people without the required cover.

Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm, so you can check them on the FCA register. Many brokers belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association, and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute. A broker must understand your demands and needs, explain key policy features and exclusions, and tell you how they are paid.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe your business and the kind of work your employees do, including any higher-risk tasks.
Say how many people you employ and whether any are part-time, temporary or seasonal.
Mention whether you already hold employers' liability cover and when it is due for renewal.
Explain whether you have made or received any claims relating to staff injuries or illness.
Note whether you work from premises, on clients' sites or from home, as this affects the cover needed.
Say where you are based so we can introduce you to a broker who works in your area.
questions: What level of employers' liability cover does the law require for a business like mine?
Which risks in my workplace would be excluded from the policy you are quoting?
How will you be paid for arranging this cover, and what will that cost me?
What should I do about displaying the certificate once the policy is in place?
How would a claim from an employee be handled, and who would I deal with?
Are you authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, and can you tell me your firm's reference?

faqs.q: Do I legally need employers' liability insurance?
faqs.a: Most UK employers are legally required to hold employers' liability insurance, and the minimum level of cover is set by law. There are limited exceptions, so it is worth asking a broker whether they apply to your situation.

faqs.q: What happens if I employ someone without cover?
faqs.a: Fines can apply if you employ people without the required employers' liability cover. Getting cover in place before staff start work avoids that risk.

faqs.q: How do I check that a broker is properly authorised?
faqs.a: Brokers and intermediaries must be authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm. You can check them on the FCA register, and complaints that are not resolved can go to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

faqs.q: Will a local broker understand my type of business?
faqs.a: A broker working in your area will often know the risks common to local trades and premises, and can explain which policy features and exclusions matter for your work. Tell them what your employees do so they can match cover to your needs.
